title: Ionic Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Ionic course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: Which part holds the main scrollable content?
questions.explanation: IonPage groups a screen, and IonContent gives it a scrolling content area. A toolbar can hold the screen title.

questions.question: What changes the count here?
questions.explanation: IonButton is a button component with Ionic styles. Its click handler can update local React state.

questions.question: Which component represents one list row?
questions.explanation: IonList groups list rows. IonItem supplies row layout, and IonLabel holds its text.

questions.question: What belongs inside IonCardContent?
questions.explanation: An Ionic card groups a title and related content. It works well for a single book or short notice.

questions.question: Where is the typed value in this Ionic event?
questions.explanation: IonInput can manage a typed value with React state. onIonInput provides the latest text through event.detail.value.

questions.question: Which value identifies the science option?
questions.explanation: IonSelect offers a controlled list of choices. onIonChange gives the selected value.

questions.question: Which event detail gives its boolean state?
questions.explanation: IonCheckbox represents a true-or-false choice. The checked value in its change event tells the current state.

questions.question: What does sizeMd="6" mean?
options: Half of a 12-part row from md upwards
questions.explanation: Ionic's grid uses rows and columns. A column can use a different share of the row at a wider breakpoint.

questions.question: Why handle onDidDismiss?
options: To keep React open state in step with the dismissed toast
questions.explanation: A toast is a short status message that appears briefly. Its open state should stay connected to React state.

questions.question: What should every simple modal make clear?
options: Its purpose and how to close it
questions.explanation: A modal is a focused layer above a page. Control its open state and give it a clear way to close.

questions.question: Should an empty list use a loading spinner forever?
options: No, it should explain that there are no items
Yes, empty and loading always mean the same thing
questions.explanation: Loading, empty and failed are different states. A spinner can show activity while words explain what the app is waiting for.

questions.question: What should be tested before optional native packaging?
questions.explanation: Ionic uses web code. A browser build can be tested before optional native packaging with tools such as Capacitor.
